## 10. Progression

### 10.1 Start state

**Since milestone 87 the game starts with nothing built.** The six colonists — four
workers, an engineer and a biologist — stand outside beside the **ship** at `(0, 0)` —
structure 0, not a building ([§6.2](#inside-and-outside--milestone-87)) — with its
cargo: **60 Water, 100 Food, 60 Ore, 189 Metal, 137 Bioplastic, 12 Spares**, and a
population cap of 6, the crew, since there is no Control dome yet. Until the first
Storage dome the hold is the storage: 500 for everything but Water, 498 of it the
cargo ([§6.5](#storage-at-milestone-122)); 468 until milestone 133 added 30 Bioplastic
([below](#bioplastic-for-the-start-at-milestone-133)). Until milestone 120
it was four colonists, 40 Food, 4 Spares and a cap of 4
([below](#the-scripted-player-at-milestone-120)). The first thing the player builds is the first dome, from
outside, and the second is the airlock that lets anyone into it. The rest of this
section is the colony the game started with until milestone 86, which is still how
most tests start ([below](#beside-the-ship-at-milestone-87)).

Until then: at `(0,0)`, on guaranteed flat foundation (ground since milestone 94): a landing pad, one small **Oxygen** dome with
one `mach_oxygen`, one small **Quarters**, one small **Storage**, and the corridors
joining them. Since milestone 86, also an **airlock** north of the Oxygen dome, at
`(0, −10)` in half tiles, with its own short corridor
([§9.3](#airlocks-are-the-doors-at-milestone-86)): structures join airlocks and other
structures now, never domes, and without one the first pump or mine would have had
nothing to join but the pad. Four colonists: two workers, one engineer, one biologist. Starting stock:
60 Water, 40 Food, **60 Ore, 75 Metal, 45 Bioplastic**, 4 Spares.

Enough to live about two sols without doing anything, which is exactly how long it
should take to realise you need power before you need anything else.

**The metal and bioplastic were 30 and 10, and that bought exactly one building.**
A colony that lives needs **three**: a solar panel (15 Metal) for oxygen by day, a
collector (14) for the 40% of the sol that has no sun
([§6.10](#610-events-and-hazards)), and an extractor (22) for water — 51 Metal, and
at the time 26 Bioplastic as well, because everything was priced in both. With 30 and
10 the player bought one building and it did not matter which: every line ended
before sol 5. 55 and 30 bought all three and left 4 and 4, which is not a fourth
building.

**It is now 60 Ore / 75 Metal / 45 Bioplastic, and the extra buys a Factory.** The
opening has to afford one thing more than survival — the dome that turns ore into
metal — or the colony is playing out of its allowance for ever
([§15](#15-open-risks) said so, and this is the measurement that closes it). At the
step-27 catalogue a panel, an extractor and a small Factory cost **57 Metal and 10
Bioplastic**, leaving 18 Metal; and those 18 are the point. Measured at ×4 over eight
sols (`tools/balance.py`, scenario 6), the Factory ate the whole 60 Ore by sol 4 and
turned it into **30 Metal — 18 → 48**, two Ore to one Metal. 48 is a mine (30) and
change, so the mine is bought out of production rather than out of the start state,
and from there the loop is closed: mine → Ore → `mach_iron` → Metal → mine.

The 60 Ore is there for exactly that reason. Without it the Factory has nothing to
eat until a mine is standing, and the mine is the thing the Factory is supposed to
pay for.

**And since milestone 31 the opening has a place in it, not just a shopping list.**
The extractor goes where the water is and the mine where the vein is
([§6.5](#65-economy)), so the first thing the player does with the cursor is look at
the map they were given. The start colony itself needs nothing of the sort — pad,
Oxygen, Quarters, Storage — and [§5.6](#56-feature-anchors) guarantees both materials
within 30 tiles of the centre; in this seed they are 4 and 7 tiles out, which is one
screen of scrolling.

**Measured, at ×4, eight sols, with nobody touching the controls afterwards**
(`tools/balance.py`, which builds through the real menu and then watches; since
milestone 45 it also fits every dome it builds through the fitting screen, round
robin over the room's list — what the dome used to do by itself — and the opening's
lines come out byte for byte as at milestone 44):

| The player builds | First death | Of what |
|---|---|---|
| nothing | **sol 2** | oxygen — 54 Water and 36 Food still in store |
| a solar panel | sol 7 | thirst, then hunger; life support runs in daylight |
| panel + collector | sol 5 | thirst — but oxygen never drops, day or night |
| panel + turbine | sol 5 | thirst — the same answer by the other route |
| panel + extractor | **none in 8 sols** | Water reaches 247, Food is gone by sol 6 |
| panel + collector + extractor | **none in 8 sols** | Food gone by sol 7 and still nobody dead — Water 373 and climbing, battery full |
| panel + extractor + small **Factory** | **none in 8 sols** | Ore 60 → 0 by sol 4, Metal 18 → **48**; Food gone by sol 6 and nobody dead by sol 8 |
| greenhouse + lab + canteen (with the materials given) | **none in 8 sols** | **The first colony that feeds itself**: Food 46 → **68** by sol 6 and 60 at sol 8, four colonists eating out of it the whole way. Water is the new tight one — 71 → 5, because every pot drinks. At milestone 45, with the domes fitted through the new screen: Food 41 → **61** by sol 4 and 50 at sol 8, Water 63 → 5, nobody dead |
| the same, plus two colonist ships — **twelve people** | **sol 6** | **Re-measured at milestone 45, and identical at 44** — the first death falls on the same frame, 24,426, in both builds. Water is gone by sol 2 and Food by sol 5. This row used to read "none in 8 sols; Food dips to 0 around sol 5 and climbs back to 26"; when that stopped being true was not tracked, which is the argument for re-running the table at each milestone that touches the economy |

Every line that solves water used to end at the same wall: **Food**, which needs a
greenhouse and a `mach_food`, which needs a dome that can be given a room. Rooms are
built ([§9.3](#93-build-flow)) and the chain runs — with the slot order fixed
([§6.5](#65-economy)) a greenhouse grows Starch *and* Vegetables, a Lab makes
Vitromeat, and `tools/balance.py` shows Food climbing **34 → 38** in a colony that is
eating out of it at the same time.

**The wall looked like people and was a bug.** That same run used to lose everyone
from sol 2 with 37 Food in the warehouse, and the reading was "four colonists cannot
staff seven machines and also eat". They could: they were being sent back to work
every time they set off for the canteen ([§6.6](#66-needs)). With that fixed the
colony runs the full eight sols with nobody dead and Food climbing again by sol 8.

**And then the chain itself was measured, and three things were wrong with it**
([§6.5](#65-economy), [§6.7](#67-jobs)): a greenhouse demanded one biologist per pot,
`mach_vitromeat` matched the canteen exactly instead of leaving headroom, and every
`Operate` job had the same priority so the nearest dome took everyone and the canteen
was never staffed. With those three fixed, the same twelve-person colony that used to
be wiped out by sol 5 **survives the full eight sols**, its store dipping to zero and
recovering. It has no margin: one chain feeds twelve only if nothing goes wrong, and
the honest advice is a second canteen — which the HUD now asks for out loud
([§9.2](#92-hud)).

That is the shape [§10.1](#101-start-state) always claimed and never had: before the
economy got a clock ([§6.5](#65-economy)) the answer was "sol 1½, of thirst, whatever
you build".

**Written** (`src/newgame.asm`), with three departures from the paragraph above.
The three domes sit 8 tiles apart centre to centre, because that is the closest
spacing that leaves a whole number of corridor tiles between two small domes
([§9.4](#94-corridor-routing)); **the pad is joined by an outdoor edge, not a
corridor**, because a corridor record can only name domes; and the third dome is a
**Canteen, not a Storage**, because the needs pass looks for exactly three room types
([§6.6](#66-needs)) and without a canteen nobody ever eats or drinks — the two sols
above would have been spent dying of thirst beside full tanks. Storage is the room no
pass reads yet, so it was the cheapest one to give up.

**And the Quarters came with a medbay fixture in them.** `mach_beds` wants an
operator and produces **nothing** — it is furniture that makes a *medbay* work, and
`room_machines` never puts it in a Quarters, so no dome the player builds has one. The
start state hand-placed one anyway, and because the job board cannot tell a useless
post from a useful one, **one of the four colonists spent 96% of the game making
beds** while the canteen next door waited for a cook. Sleep is satisfied by the room,
not by the beds ([§6.6](#66-needs)), so the machine is simply gone.

**And for a while the Quarters were a second oxygen generator.** `ob_domeadr`
destroys `DE`, which is where the setup loop was holding the machine id, so every
dome in the start state was given machine 0. Nothing looked wrong — sleep is
satisfied by the *room*, not by the beds — but life support drank twice the water and
demanded twice the power, and that is the whole of the opening's balance. It was
found by measuring the colony's curve, not by reading the loop.

The table that matters most is the job board: **its empty value is 255 and zero
means `J_BUILD`**, so a board that was never initialised reads as thirty-two Build
jobs and the build mode finds nowhere to post. Colonists likewise start with every
need at 255 — starting at zero kills them before they can walk to the fridge.

The generator is **not** part of this binary ([§4.2](#42-the-eight-banks)), so a
new game is two loads: generate the plane, then load the game over the generator.

#### Smaller, at milestone 74

`src/newgame.asm` went from 670 bytes to **394**, and bank 2's code area from 888
bytes free to **1,164**. A new game got 1.7 ms faster. That is the same in every case,
and it is all `game_new`'s own part: the rest of the 480 ms is `ui_init`'s first full
redraw.

- **One flow.** `ng_wipe`, `ng_colony`, `ng_people` and `ng_stock` were four routines
  with one caller each, and `ng_stamp`, `ng_ff` and `ng_full` were called from inside
  them. `game_new` is now one body, in the same order.
- **Bank 6's five tables are one block.** The agents, the node occupancy, the domes,
  the structures and the corridors sit end to end from `&6C00` to `&7DE0`. One `ldir`
  clears them where five did, and four `assert`s hold the layout to that.
- **The three agent columns that start at 255 are one loop.** They are the +128
  halves of three consecutive pages — the ring slot, the edge and the task — so the
  fill moves on with `set 7,l` after each one.
- **Only what is not zero is written.** The tables are clear when the colony goes in,
  so a dome's power and operators are left alone instead of being written as 0.
- **The domes and the pad share a template.** A dome record and a structure record
  both begin with `cx`, `cy` and two bytes (size and room, or kind and size),
  followed by the state and 255. So four rows of four bytes describe all four sites,
  and `ngc_rec` writes each one.
  - The stamp reads the same table: each site's 4 × 4 starts at centre / 2 − 2. The
    separate list of rectangles is gone.
  - So is the template's machine column, which held `NO_MACH` for two domes out of
    three. The one machine, the first dome's oxygen generator, is two stores.
- **The stamp takes `tile_addr` once a site** and steps 128 bytes a row. Its four
  variables are gone.
- **Both corridors come from one loop**, and the graph's three edges from
  `cr_link_bc`. This is a label inside `route.asm`'s `cr_link` that takes `B` and `C`
  and adds both directions. It ends in `rt_mark`, which a new game calls anyway:
  `wheel_reset` clears `rt_dirty`, and `game_new`'s own `rt_mark` sets it again.
- **The stocks and the clock are pairs.** Each is the low byte of an address in the
  economy's page and a value, for the 17 bytes that are not zero. Each pair is
  `assert`ed to the page.
  - Two macros, `NG_BYTE` and `NG_WORD`, name the fields.
  - The old table of fourteen stocks was half zeros, and ten more stores set the
    clock, the random seed and the flags.

The check was a script kept out of the repository, on `build/main.sna`. It ran the
game for 400 frames and then called `game_new` from 40 starting states:

- the first as the game left it;
- the other 39 with random bytes in everything `game_new` clears or writes: bank 6
  from the agents to `&7FFF`, bank 2 from the economy to the end of the graph, and the
  whole world plane.

It compared every byte that changed in all eight banks, and all 40 were identical.

**What the planted faults found.** Thirty-six faults were run against the script and
fourteen tests that start from `game_new`:

- `test_game.py`, `test_loop.py`, `test_needs.py`, `test_power.py`,
  `test_balance.py`, `test_save.py` and `test_map.py`;
- `test_build.py`, `test_meteor.py`, `test_fit.py`, `test_sound.py`,
  `test_reveal.py`, `test_speed.py` and `test_disc.py`.

- **One changes nothing.** Not writing `cr_a` back to 0 before the second corridor
  is the same program: both corridors leave from dome 0, so `cr_plan` never swaps the
  ends. The script found every byte the same. The write stays, for a start colony
  whose second corridor does not.
- **The script caught the other thirty-five.**
- **The fourteen tests together caught seventeen.** `test_game.py` caught fourteen,
  `test_power.py` twelve, `test_save.py` eight, `test_meteor.py` seven. `test_map.py`,
  `test_build.py` and `test_speed.py` caught none. The eighteen they let through:
  - **all five faults in the stamp**: no foundation under the pad, every site one
    tile east, bit 3 kept, the next row 64 bytes on, three rows instead of four. None
    of the fourteen looks at the plane under the start colony;
  - the second corridor: its record not written, or its tiles never stamped;
  - each wipe one byte short: the economy, the graph, the bank-6 block, and the last
    job slot;
  - integrity 254, and the oxygen generator at 100 health;
  - the colonists not indoors, without a destination, or with the third page of
    needs empty;
  - the last economy pair (the population cap) missing;
  - `wheel_reset` left out.
- **`tests/test_newgame.py` catches all thirty-five** that change anything.

`tests/test_newgame.py` calls `game_new` directly in `main.sna` from eight starts:

- the game as it runs;
- seven with garbage in everything `game_new` clears or writes, and in the whole
  plane.

It checks the result against [§10.1](#101-start-state) written from the prose, not
from the Z80:

- **The economy**: cleared, except for the stocks, the clock, the seed, the flags, the
  living and the cap. The five meteor bytes past the cleared 86 are left alone.
- **The job board**: every slot `NO_JOB`, and nothing else in it touched.
- **The graph**: 0–1, 0–2, 2–64 and, since milestone 86, 0–65 (the airlock), both
  ways, and no other degree.
- **Bank 6's block**: clear, except for the three domes and their one machine, the
  pad, the airlock, the three corridors, the three agent columns at 255, and four
  colonists. Their needs are full and their ring slots come from `corr_fill`.
- **The world**: foundation and occupancy under the four sites and the airlock's 2×2,
  with the decor kept.
  The corridors' tiles get occupancy alone, as `cr_stamp` gives them; the tiles come
  from `tools/route.py` and `tiles_of`. Nothing else changes.
- **`rt_dirty` and `wh_slot`.**

It holds the whole call, `ui_init`'s first redraw included, to no slower than this
milestone measured; milestone 73's file fails. Its four negatives are:

- two agent columns at 255 instead of three;
- three rows of foundation;
- one economy pair fewer;
- the needs on two pages.

**Two things the test's own first runs got wrong:**

- **A corridor is not foundation.** The rule first stamped the corridors' tiles like
  the domes'. `cr_stamp` sets occupancy only, as [§9.4](#94-corridor-routing) says it
  should: concrete under a diagonal would paint four times what the corridor stands
  on.
- **The figure cache is not `game_new`'s.** It sits right after the corridor table in
  bank 6, and `ui_init`'s first redraw rebuilds it. The check stops at the table's
  end.

#### Beside the ship, at milestone 87

The user's choices: the ship carries **today's stocks plus what the old start colony
was worth, without the landing pad** — three small domes (36 Metal, 24 Bioplastic),
the oxygen generator (8, 2), ten corridor tiles (60, 30) and the airlock (10, 6), so
Metal 75 → **189** and Bioplastic 45 → **107**, **137** since milestone 133. The pad (45) is
built later, for ships.
Water and food need a canteen from the start, as before; outside, the four breathe
from suits that last ten minutes (milestone 90, [§6.6](#suits-at-milestone-90)).

`game_new` (`src/newgame.asm`, 442 → **289** bytes) wipes as before, writes the ship
record and the occupancy of its 2×2 (no foundation: it landed, nobody built under it),
and puts the four at node 64 with `F_ALIVE` alone. The graph has no edges at all.

**Measured from the empty start** (scratch scenarios through the real menu, as
`tools/balance.py` builds; the four have the same needs and move together, so they
mostly die together):

| The player builds | First death | Of what |
|---|---|---|
| nothing | sol 1.72 (1.75 before the suits), all four | thirst — there is no canteen. Their suits had 74 units left, three minutes: thirst comes first |
| a Canteen and its airlock | sol 1.72 (1.67), three | **oxygen, inside** — they went in to drink and stayed in a dome with no generator |
| an Oxygen dome fitted, a Canteen, the airlock, a solar panel | sol 4.42 (4.33), all four | oxygen at night: no power, no generator |
| the same and a collector | sol 5.05 (5), all four | thirst — Water 60 → 0 by sol 4.5, oxygen full all the way |

Measured again at milestone 90, with the suits (`tests/test_suit.py`'s world, the
same builds, at ×4): nobody died of a suit. Those who reached a minute outside
while building walked back to the airlock and went on from there, and the four
dates moved by a few hundredths of a sol, the walks back being the difference.

The last two are milestone 86's "panel" and "panel + collector" lines, with the
domes built rather than given: the opening has the same shape, and the cargo pays
for it with 94 Metal and 71 Bioplastic left — an extractor (22) is the next thing.
The second line was the interim rule showing: until the suits of milestone 90, the
safest place without a generator was outside. Now it is for ten minutes.

**The old colony is a test fixture now.** Most tests need domes, corridors and people
inside to test anything, and building them through the menu would make every one of
them a scenario. So the old start lives on as `src/colony.asm`, in
`build/main.sna` but not on the disc. Until milestone 90 it was assembled after
`zz_bank0_end`; since 91 it is in **the last page of the ghost's log** (`GH_BUF`,
bank 2, just under `PAGE2_CODE`), outside `game2.bin` as it was outside `game.bin`,
and bank 0's code took its place. Since milestone 158 it is under the start's code and
`game_new`, which took the log's last 448 bytes and are in `game2.bin`
([§4.2](#the-start-in-the-ghosts-log-at-milestone-158)); the colony is still outside it. The cursor writes the log from its start, so only a
very large ghost reaches that page, and a `game_new` of the colony after one would
not find it — no test does that. `tests/test_game.py` writes `build/colony.sna`, the same snapshot with the
byte `ng_colony` set, and `game_new` jumps to the fixture when it is. Nineteen tests
start from it directly, more through `test_place.py` and `test_reveal.py`, and so does
`tools/balance.py`; it sets the airlock's `ST_JOINED`, puts the four
inside, and sets the stocks and cap of milestone 86 (75, 45, 8). An `assert` keeps
it inside that page. **Since milestone 132 `colony.sna` also lays a vein** in its bank 4:
the rock at x = −13, y −4 … 1, at the edge of the western ridge, becomes mountain with
ore (`COLONY_VEIN` in `tools/balance.py`; its colony helpers see it through
`colony_plane`, and `tests/test_game.py` stops if those tiles are not rock). With the
wider plateau ([§5.5](#a-wider-plateau-at-milestone-132)) the ridge's own vein is two
tiles of rock away from the ground, and the only two places beside a vein fall on the
colony's pad; the mine tests measure the drilling, not the generator. `main.sna`, the
game, keeps the generator's world.

**`tests/test_newgame.py` checks both**, each from the prose: the empty start
(economy, an empty graph, the ship's record and occupancy, four outside) and the
fixture (the old rule, with `ST_JOINED`). Its negatives are now two agent columns, the
ship with one row of occupancy, the colonists inside, one economy pair fewer, the needs
on two pages, and — on the fixture — three rows of foundation and the airlock without
`ST_JOINED`. A new game with `ui_init`'s first redraw takes **249,931 µs**, half the
480,535 of milestone 74: there is nothing to draw (**249,986** since milestone 88,
which clears the whole economy, 92 bytes instead of 86).

#### The scripted player, at milestone 120

Every number in this section until now was measured on scenarios: a few buildings
placed and then watched. **`tools/play.py` plays the game**: `main.sna` as the player
gets it, built from the empty start with the player's keys — the build menu, a
placement the reach rule accepts ([§9.3](#93-build-flow)), `FIT` slot by slot, `C` and
`FIRE` for a colonist ship — at ×4 for twenty sols. A plan is a list of steps, each
waiting until its materials are in store and what it needs is finished, with no more
than two sites open; it goes where `tools/reach.py` says the fewest corridor pieces
are, near its target (water and ore for the extractor and the mine). Every eighth of a
sol it samples the stocks, power, sites, jobs and every colonist's needs, and it logs
deaths with their cause, machines that break, buildings that are hit, storms and ships.
`--make` builds a snapshot for any seed and planet, with `G_worldinfo` written as the
disc's generator leaves it, so each world has its own events
([§6.10](#the-same-disasters-in-every-game-until-milestone-120)); `--tweak` pokes the
cargo or the fault roll for an experiment. Twelve worlds — seeds `ACE1`, `1048` and
`BEEF` on all four planets — take about fifteen minutes in parallel.

**What it found at milestone 119.** No colony reached sol 14, whatever the plan:

| Plan | How it ended |
|---|---|
| Planetbase's order: panel, oxygen, airlock, extractor, canteen, battery, mine, factory, a medium greenhouse, lab, meals | **all four in the canteen from sol 2 holding `T_NEED`**, nobody at the sites — a need without its room ([§6.6](#a-need-without-its-room-at-milestone-120)). Fixed, it lived to sol 11.4–12.2: the four Spares were gone by sol 10, the oxygen generator broke, a meteor shower took the airlock |
| the same with small greenhouses (one plant, no corridor for the medium one) | 12 worlds: everyone dead between sol 6.2 and 11.6 — oxygen, inside, after the generator broke with no Spare |
| a Spares factory straight after the Metal one | dead by sol 13: the `SPARES` machine turned all the Metal and Bioplastic into 47 Spares, Metal sat at 3 for eight sols, and the food chain was never paid for |
| the mine straight after the factory, no Spares factory | dead at sol 13, of hunger: three operators for six posts ([§6.7](#67-jobs): `Operate` is workers' and biologists', three of the four), so the Meat and Metal machines stood idle |
| Control and pad first, ships as soon as there is room | eight colonists and 40 Food: dead of hunger by sol 7 |

**The levers, measured** (the mine-first plan, `ACE1` and `BEEF`, planet 0):

| Changed | How it ended |
|---|---|
| 12 Spares | dead at sol 13, hunger |
| 12 Spares, 250 Metal | dead at sol 12.3 — the meteor shower at 10.5 took the airlock with two outside |
| no malfunctions at all | dead at sol 13, hunger |
| malfunctions 1 in 256, 8 Spares | dead at sol 12.3 |
| the engineer allowed to `Operate` | worse: dead at 11.2–12.3, the only engineer locked into a machine while the generator waited for repair |
| 12 Spares and 80 Food | **alive at sol 20**, both worlds — with 4 Food and no Spares left |
| 12 Spares, 100 Food, malfunctions 1 in 256 | **alive at sol 20**, both worlds |

**The user chose**: 12 Spares and malfunctions 1 in 256
([§6.10](#how-often-measured)), 100 Food, the events seeded from the world
([§6.10](#the-same-disasters-in-every-game-until-milestone-120)), and **a crew of six**
— two more workers — rather than leaving it to the first ship or capping production.
The crew's cap is the base of the population cap, `POP_BASE` 6
([§6.11](#611-ships-and-arrivals)). The test colony keeps its four, its 40 Food and its
4 Spares (`ng_econ_col`, and a 255 that ends each crew list — one byte of the ghost's
log page, 4 left).

**What it found at milestone 120**, with those numbers, after one more fix it showed
on the way: a dome sealed with its builders outside a finished airlock left them
standing outside on the airlock's node, where the suit's "back to the nearest airlock"
never moves anyone — the engineer died there at sol 4.27, and the colony with him when
the generator broke ([§6.2](#inside-and-outside--milestone-87)). The plan without a
Spares factory, on twelve worlds:

| Worlds | At sol 20 |
|---|---|
| `ACE1` 0, 2, 3 · `BEEF` 0, 2, 3 | **6 of 6 alive** |
| `ACE1` 1 · `BEEF` 1 | 4 of 6: hunger from sol 19.2, the water planet leaving room for too few domes near the ship |
| `1048` 0–3 | dead or one alive at sol 19.2: the scripted player never found a place for the mine within reach, the 60 Ore of the cargo became 30 Metal and then nothing, and the twelve Spares were spent by sol 16 — the next break of the generator was everyone |

**What is left**, in [§15](#15-open-risks): Metal has a trap — with the cargo's Ore
gone and less than 30 Metal in store, nothing buys a mine again, and nothing makes a
Spare without Metal; production has no limit, so a Spares machine eats the colony's
Metal; the three draws of a revolution still bring their disasters in bursts. And the
scripted player is not a good player: it builds in a fixed order, does not chain
buildings toward ore that is out of reach, and its plan with ships starves. The user's
answers came at milestones 121–124 ([below](#the-balance-measured-at-milestone-124)).

#### The balance, measured, at milestone 124

After milestone 120 the user asked for five things:

- Metal that never runs out for good: a mine anywhere, milestone 123.
- A limit on production: the storage only, milestone 122.
- Disasters random and sparse, none before twenty colonists: milestone 121.
- Storage capacity: milestone 122.
- **This: measure the balance and design it.**

The scripted player
([above](#the-scripted-player-at-milestone-120)) played each rule on the same twelve
worlds, `ACE1`, `1048` and `BEEF` on the four planets, for **40 sols** at ×4. It used a
longer plan, `long`:

- **`store`.** `mine_ns`, plus a Storage S dome whenever the goods come within 120 of
  the capacity and no such dome is being built.
- **`long`.** `store` without its ship step, then:
  - a ship whenever the oxygen domes have room for ten more each;
  - a second and third oxygen dome, quarters, greenhouses, a lab, a canteen and a
    third solar panel, as the colony passes 7 to 15 colonists.
- **Mines.** The player knows the free mine. When it finds no place near a vein, it
  puts the mine beside one of its buildings at half yield
  ([§6.5](#a-mine-anywhere-at-milestone-123)). 7 of the 12 worlds did that.
- **Samples.** Each now carries the capacity, the full flag and the mines' flags.
  `--json` writes the samples and the events for charts, and `--tweak iron=N` sets the
  METAL recipe's output.

**The storage rule decided everything:**

| When the storage is full | Alive at sol 40 | Deaths | What happened |
|---|---|---|---|
| every machine that makes a stock stops (milestones 122–123) | **2 of 12** | 60, all hunger | three worlds starved at sol 19–20 (below); seven more between sol 33.5 and 38.7, full of Starch, Vegetables and Ore with `MEALS` and `METAL` stopped |
| only what adds to the store stops (milestone 124, [§6.5](#only-what-adds-to-the-store-stops-at-milestone-124)) | **9 of 12** | 18, all hunger | only the three worlds below |

**The three worlds that die under either rule** are `ACE1` and `BEEF` on the water
planet and `1048` on planet 2. None of them died of the rules. The scripted player
never found room for its greenhouses within reach, so the cargo's 100 Food lasted to
sol 19, as at milestone 120. `ACE1` on the water planet never placed a mine either.

**What a colony of six does in 40 sols**, with milestone 124's rule:

- **It does not grow.** No colony built the landing pad, which costs 45 Metal, so no
  ship came.
- **Metal stayed scarce.** After sol 3 it was under 10 in 23–80% of the samples.
- **Ore was not what held it back.** On a vein (`BEEF` 0), Ore piled up to 140 while
  Metal stayed under 25. The METAL machine needs an operator. Only workers and
  biologists may `Operate`, and they also dig, haul, build and run the canteen, the
  lab and the plastic. Off a vein (`ACE1` 0), Ore ran short as well: one driller makes
  1 a cycle.
- **The storage is full a third to a half of the time from sol ~12.** It was full in
  27–51% of the samples. Only three Storage domes were built in twelve worlds, because
  the player spends its Metal before it reaches a dome's price.

**One lever, measured: Metal twice as fast** (`--tweak iron=2`, 2 Ore into 2 Metal):

| METAL makes | Alive at sol 40 | Largest colony | Ships | Deaths |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (the game) | 9 of 12 | 6 everywhere | none | 18, hunger |
| 2 | 9 of 12 | 18–20 in three worlds | in those three, the first at sol 22–36 | 64: 38 hunger, 26 air |

The colonies that grew died the way the scripted player plays.

- In `ACE1` 3 the player counts oxygen domes, not working generators. It let in 18
  colonists, whom two generators held only while both ran. One stood idle in half the
  samples, giving 20 of the 32 needed instead of 40, and 16 died at sol 34.2. Four
  more ships came, and 17 more died by sol 40.
- In `BEEF` 3 the colony grew faster than its greenhouses. The second ones came at sol
  34.4 and 38.3, and 11 of 20 starved from sol 36.9.

No colony reached twenty colonists before sol 37.5, so no disaster fell in any game.
The disasters were measured on the reference instead, and that is how the storm's roll
was found never to pass the calm
([§6.10](#the-storms-that-never-came-found-at-milestone-124)).

**What was changed, and what was not:**

- **Changed:** only what adds to the store stops (a fix, not a tuning), and the two
  rolls of the disasters.
- **Not changed:** the METAL machine's output. The measurement offers it to the user:
  with 2, three colonies of twelve reach twenty colonists by sol 40. With 1, none
  grows. **The user chose 2, at milestone 125** ([below](#twice-the-metal-at-milestone-125)).
- **Still open** ([§15](#15-open-risks)): operators bind before Ore does, and a
  `SPARES` machine with Metal to eat still eats all of it.

#### Twice the Metal, at milestone 125

The user chose the lever that milestone 124 measured. `mach_iron` makes **2 Metal from
2 Ore**, where it made 1. The change is one number in `tools/econ.py`'s `RECIPE`, which
`tools/pack.py` writes into the recipe table, so it costs no byte and no µs.

The machine still needs its operator. Two Ore for two Metal neither adds to the store
nor frees room, so it is not `MF_ADDS`, and it keeps going when the storage is full
([§6.5](#only-what-adds-to-the-store-stops-at-milestone-124)).

**Measured on the game as built, not with the tweak.** These are the same twelve
worlds and plan as above, 40 sols, from snapshots made by the milestone 125 binary:

| METAL makes | Alive at sol 40 | Largest colony | Worlds with ships | Deaths |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (milestone 124) | 9 of 12 | 6 everywhere | none | 18, hunger |
| 2 (`--tweak iron=2` on milestone 124) | 9 of 12 | 18–20 in three worlds | 3 | 64: 38 hunger, 26 air |
| 2 (milestone 125) | 9 of 12 | 18–20 in three worlds | 3 | 64: 38 hunger, 26 air |

**The same game as the tweak.** Every event (buildings, ships, faults and deaths) is the same in all twelve worlds. In three worlds a few samples fall a frame or two apart, and one sample has stocks 2–4 apart. A colony of six whose mine is off a vein (`ACE1` 0) builds its pad at sol 35.4 and grows to 18 by sol 40. Two others (`ACE1` 3, `BEEF` 3) have their first ship at sol 22. The other six survivors stay at six or fewer: their Metal still goes on domes and corridors before it reaches the pad's 45. The three that starve at sol 19–20 are the three without greenhouses, as before.

The deaths of the colonies that grow are the scripted player's: it counts oxygen domes
rather than working generators, and its food plan lags its ships. Three colonies of
six reach the landing pad now, and none did at milestone 124. That is what the lever
was for.

#### The scripted player counts air, at milestone 127

From milestone 124 the plan `long` let a ship in whenever its oxygen domes had room for
ten more each. That counted rooms, not generators. In `ACE1` 3 one of the two generators
often had no operator, giving 20 of the 32 needed, and 33 colonists died. A ship now
comes (`ship_ok`, `tools/play.py`) only when all of these hold:

- there is room under the cap, as before;
- **the oxygen actually made**, at its lowest over the last sol, covers everyone plus
  the ship's four;
- **the Meals in store** cover five sols for all of them;
- the Meals have not fallen over the last sol.

The game is unchanged; this is the measuring tool. The twelve worlds, plan `long`, 40
sols, with milestones 125–127 in the game:

| | Milestone 126, the old rule | Milestone 127, `ship_ok` |
|---|---|---|
| Alive at sol 40 | 9 of 12 | 9 of 12 |
| Largest colony | 10–20 in four worlds | 10 in four worlds, the first ship at sol 21–35 |
| Deaths | 135 | 18, all hunger |

**No colony died of growing.** The 18 deaths are the three worlds that never found a place for their greenhouses, as since milestone 124. Four colonies took one ship and stopped at ten. With ten, their Meals fell by about 50 over 14 sols (`BEEF` 3: 98 → 47), so the rule held the next ship. The scripted player now grows only as fast as its own food and air, which is slower than the game allows. With ten, its second greenhouses come late or not at all: one more Starch dome at sol 27–33, after which 1 Bioplastic was left, and no second Vegetables dome or lab. Bioplastic, not Metal, is what holds them now.

#### Past twenty, at milestone 131

The user asked for the scripted player to play longer, past twenty colonists, to find
the next real problems. Plan `long` with `ship_ok` grows no colony past ten in 40 sols,
and three of twelve starve at sol 19 ([above](#the-scripted-player-counts-air-at-milestone-127)).
So `tools/play.py` got plan **`big`**, and the measuring tweaks to look beyond it:

- **Layout** (`Game.spot_zone`):
  - a dome goes in line with one already standing, the same row or column a tile
    apart, so its corridor is one straight piece that crosses nothing. Otherwise the
    nearest place with four pieces or fewer, then any;
  - structures go together, with paths of three tiles or fewer, as far from the domes
    as twelve tiles;
  - a mine off a vein goes at the edge too.
  - "As near the centre as possible" piled domes round the ship, and after three to six
    of them every new corridor met something (`PATH BLOCKED`). A strict lattice did not
    fit narrow ground.
- **Growth from the last sol's measurements**, not fixed head counts:
  - oxygen made that does not cover everyone and four more;
  - water falling;
  - power cut by day (a Solar panel) or by night (a collector);
  - Meals falling: whichever of Starch, Vegetables and Meat is missing, or another
    kitchen;
  - Bioplastic or Metal short with their raw material in store;
  - sleep;
  - the store, as at milestone 124.
- **Pad and Control right after the food**, so that hands can come.
- **Tweaks for measuring:**
  - `feed=M:B` tops Metal and Bioplastic up to M and B at every sample;
  - `plastic=N` sets the PLASTIC machine's yield;
  - every two sols the game runs 800 frames at ×1 and 400 at ×4 and counts the
    wheel's ticks: does it keep up? Over 150 frames the count was ±7 %.

Twelve worlds (`ACE1`, `1048`, `BEEF`, planets 0–3), 40 sols:

| Batch | Plan | Alive at sol 40 | Deaths | Largest colony |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | `long` (milestone 127's, unchanged to 130) | 9 of 12 | 18 | 10, in four worlds |
| A | `big` | 9 of 12 | 18 | 10, in three |
| B | `big`, paths without occupancy | 9 of 12 | 22 | 10, in four |
| C | `big`, no occupancy, `feed=120:80`, 50 sols | **0 of 12** | **164** | **22** |
| D | `long`, PLASTIC ×2 | 9 of 12 | 30 | 14, once |
| E | `big`, no occupancy, PLASTIC ×2 | 8 of 12 | 32 | 10, in four |

**What it found:**

1. **The landing site on ice holds few domes.** In 48 worlds per planet, the 4×4 places
   on buildable ground joined to the ship within 24 tiles — the most domes S that could
   stand there, before corridors and structures:

   | Planet | Fewest | 10 % | Median | Under 12 |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | Desert | 20 | 24 | 30 | 0 of 48 |
   | Ice | **6** | **9** | **14** | **15 of 48** |
   | Storm | 12 | 16 | 25 | 0 of 48 |
   | Barren moon | 30 | 37 | 52 | 0 of 48 |

   `ACE1` 1 has 9, and three domes fitted: it starves in every plan. A plateau of 8 and
   a blend to 16, instead of 5 and 10 ([§5.5](#55-centre-plateau-and-world-rim)), gives
   ice 20 / 24 / 28 and the desert 40 / 43 / 50. **The player chose the plateau of 8 for
   every planet**: built at [milestone 132](#a-wider-plateau-at-milestone-132).

2. **A structure's path was a fence** ([§9.3](#paths-you-can-build-over-at-milestone-131)):
   built at this milestone.

3. **Bioplastic locks.** The 107 of the start go into domes and corridors, 3 a piece, and
   the factory that would make more needs Bioplastic too.
   - In B and E it is under 10 for 99 % of the time after sol 5, and the factory was built
     in 1 world of 12.
   - PLASTIC ×2 (as METAL ×2, [above](#twice-the-metal-at-milestone-125)) helps where the
     factory stands: in D, with plan `long`, the time under 10 falls from 26 % to 11 %,
     and colonist ships go from 4 to 6.
   - It does not open the lock: E is B.
   - Merchants came often in every run; the scripted player does not trade.

   **The player chose PLASTIC ×2 and more Bioplastic at the start**: built at
   [milestone 133](#bioplastic-for-the-start-at-milestone-133).

4. **Growth outruns the food.** With Metal and Bioplastic topped up (C), the colonies
   reach 10–22 colonists and every one of them starves.
   - In `BEEF` 2, at 18, the Meat is 0 from sol 13. One lab does not feed past about
     fourteen, and the second found no place within fourteen tiles of the domes.
   - The Meals fall for thirty sols.
   - A ship comes when the store covers five sols, not when production can grow with
     it.
   - This is the scripted player's limit as much as the game's. A player would build a
     lab M (four machines on 36 tiles) where an S does not fit.

5. **The speed holds.** At 21 colonists ×1 keeps 1.00 tick a frame, and ×4 keeps 3.64 or
   more.

6. **Disasters and intruders past twenty were not seen in play:** the colonies die as
   they reach it. The harness tests them ([§6.10](#610-events-and-hazards)).

**The user also asked for visitors as in Planetbase.** Today a visitor ship comes
unbidden, eats 6 Food, raises morale and leaves; the game has no money, and trade is
barter ([§6.11](#611-ships-and-arrivals)). They chose:

- visitors who pay in **coins**, a new stock that merchants take;
- landing on the **pad**;
- walking the base like colonists;
- coming as the colony's **prestige** grows.

Milestone 134 began it, with the coins and the prestige ([§6.11](#visitors-who-pay-and-prestige-at-milestone-134)); the merchant
takes and sells coins since 135 ([§6.11](#coins-at-the-merchant-at-milestone-135)), and the visitors walk at 136.

#### Bioplastic for the start, at milestone 133

The player chose both levers of milestone 131's third finding.

- **`mach_bioplastic` makes 2 Bioplastic from 2 Starch**, where it made 1: one number in
  `tools/econ.py`'s `RECIPE`, as METAL ×2 was at
  [milestone 125](#twice-the-metal-at-milestone-125). Two for two is not `MF_ADDS`, so it
  keeps working when the storage is full.
- **The ship brings 137 Bioplastic**, 30 more than 107. Not more: without Water the cargo
  is 498, and the hold takes 500 ([§6.5](#storage-at-milestone-122)). From 140 the game
  would start with `STORAGE FULL`, its gardens and drills stopped until something was
  built. The 160 first mentioned would make 521. `tests/test_newgame.py` now checks that
  the cargo fits.

**The scripted player fitted machines only with 4 Bioplastic in stock**, while a machine
costs 2 (8 Metal and 2 Bioplastic). With 2 left after its dome, the plastic factory stayed
empty for twenty sols (`BEEF` 0, from sol 12.6). It now waits for 8 and 2. The batches
below are all with that player.

Twelve worlds, plan `big`, 40 sols, after milestone 132's plateau; `--tweak plastic=N`
pokes the recipe on the game as built:

| Batch | PLASTIC | Start | Bioplastic under 10 | Plastic factory | Largest colony | Deaths |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| milestone 132 | 1 | 107 | 80 % of the time | 0 of 12 | 6 in ten worlds, 10 in two | 15 |
| `plastic=2` on 132 | 2 | 107 | 80 % | 0 of 12 | the same | 15 |
| `plastic=1` on 133 | 1 | 137 | 9 % | 12 of 12 | 10 in eleven, 18 in one | 25 |
| **milestone 133** | 2 | 137 | **4 %** | **12 of 12** | **10 in all twelve** | 25 |

**The 30 at the start open the lock; ×2 alone does nothing**, as milestone 131 found: the
factory is never built, so its recipe never runs. With 137 the factory is built in every
world between sol 11 and 21, and ×2 halves the time under 10 from there.

**Every colony now takes its first ship of colonists, and stops at ten.** All 25 deaths
are hunger, in five worlds, and one colony dies out. Metal is now the wall: in `BEEF` 0 it stays between 0 and 4
from sol 6 to sol 25, so the second lab, which would feed past ten, is never paid for. The
food falls, `ship_ok` calls no second ship, and the colony starves at sol 27. That is the
next thing to measure ([§15](#15-open-risks)): measured at
[milestone 137](#the-metal-wall-measured-at-milestone-137), and the wall is the hands.

#### The metal wall, measured, at milestone 137

Milestone 133 left every colony of the scripted player at ten, with Metal at 0–4 for
twenty sols. After the visitors (milestones 134–136), the same twelve worlds, plan `big`,
40 sols, were measured again with more in each sample: coins, prestige, goodwill and
visitors; every METAL machine and its operators; bots; open jobs by kind. A second probe
(`actmeasure.py` in the scratch directory, as at milestone 126) logged what every
colonist was doing, who was digging, and the mine's pile.

**Today, at milestone 136:** 10 of 12 alive, one colony past ten (14), 27 deaths, all
hunger, 13 colonist ships. Every colony had one mine and one METAL machine to the end.
Visitors came to every colony, two or three a ship and about seven ships each, and paid
10 a ship (15 where trees grew; the scripted player builds no lounge): 70–155 coins by
sol 40, never spent, because the scripted player does not trade.

**It is not the Metal machine, and mostly not the storage. It is the mine, and the mine
is the hands.** One digger makes 2 Ore a flow cycle, about 23 a sol. After sol 15 the
colonies got 3.4 a sol, counted from the loads taken off the mine's pile:

- **Nobody digging 47 % of the time.** Twenty per cent of each specialty gives a colony
  of ten four workers, and four workers kept the greenhouses (26 % of their time), the
  factory (21 %), the canteen (20 %), the lab (13 %) and the mine (13 %). The digger
  leaves to refill the suit, and a Drill job is open and unassigned in 91 % of the
  samples. The engineers, the medic and the guard were idle 96–97 % of the time — four
  people of ten.
- **Power short 40 % of the time**, at night: under `P_ESS` only life support runs, so
  the mine, the METAL machine and the Meals stop together.
- **The store full 36 % of the time**, with Starch (150–200), Vegetables (about 100) and

#### The balance, fixed, at milestone 138

After milestone 137 the user asked what was left, and then to fix the balance. The
scripted player was measured again, and most of what it found first was the player's.

**The scripted player's fixes** (`tools/play.py`, plan `big`):

- **Power before everything else that grows.** With the food first, a 15 Metal solar
  panel waited behind a 20 Metal canteen that could not be paid. Then the power ran
  short by day too, 36 against 50–56 in `BEEF` 3, and the Meals stopped half the time.
  The colonists starved with 190 Starch, 120 Vegetables and 74 Meat in store. Every
  machine but life support stops when the power is short.
- **A night that empties a battery that never filled wants a panel, not a collector.**
  Every power building is the large one: a panel makes 18, a collector holds 360. With
  two panels against a demand of 28–35 the day left nothing to store, and the player
  built collectors in a row, five in `1048` 0. It now builds a panel unless the battery
  reached 90 % in the last sol.
- **A colonist ship only when the Meals rise** by four a sol, about what four more eat,
  or cover ten sols. "Not falling" let the ship come to a canteen that fed six.
- **The Storage dome after food and power, not last.** Last, every step it could not pay
  held it back, and no world of twelve built one.
- **Deaths while intruders are about are named as theirs.** `cause()` read the needs
  and called a death with water at 200 "thirst".
- Each sample also keeps production, demand, the battery and its capacity, the
  structures and the domes.
- **Twenty-four worlds, not twelve.** The seeds `5A5A`, `2024` and `C0DE` were added: a
  batch of twelve moved by one to three worlds with the player's choices, as much as

#### The scripted player trades, at milestone 139

After milestone 138 the colonies held 70–155 coins at sol 40, and the scripted player
had never traded with a merchant. The user asked for it to learn. Only
`tools/play.py` changed. The game is the same, and with trading turned off
(tweak `notrade`) a batch matches milestone 138's event for event.

**Through the line, as a player does it**
([§6.11](#coins-at-the-merchant-at-milestone-135)):

1. `T`, then `M`, from the look mode.
2. For each good, `RIGHT` until `tr_g` is that good, then `UP` or `DOWN` until its
   byte in `TR_NET` holds the amount. The script checks after every key.
3. `SPACE`.

It trades once per merchant (`EC_LANDS`), as soon as one has landed. The script reads
`EC_SHSTATE` and `EC_SHKIND` live, not from the last sample. The first version read
the sample. In `2024` 0 a visitors' ship left and a merchant arrived between two
samples, so the script tried to trade with a merchant still in the air. A failed
attempt now records why: the line did not open, the line did not take the amounts,
or `SPACE` made no deal.

**What it takes**, in this order, while the budget lasts (its coins and its surplus).
The prices are the merchant's: value plus markup.

1. Metal, up to 200.
2. Ore, up to 60, while Metal is under 100 and a METAL machine stands. A machine
   turns 2 Ore into 2 Metal, and Ore costs 10 against Metal's 15.
3. Guns, up to three, once there are twelve colonists. Intruders come at twenty.
4. Spares, up to ten.
5. Bioplastic, up to 40.
6. Food, when there is less than five a colonist.

**What it gives**, until what it gives is worth at least what it takes:

1. Coins first, since they do nothing else.
2. Then whatever is over a reserve, the largest value first, in the merchant's lots.
   The reserves are 60 Bioplastic, 20 Medicinal plants, and six a colonist (at least
   60) for each of Starch, Vegetables and Meat.

**Measured** on 24 worlds over 40 sols. The row without trading is the same script
with the tweak `notrade` (`nt139`), the same as `f138`:

| | Alive | Past ten | Past twenty | Largest | Mean at sol 40 | Deaths | Colonist ships | Power short | Store full | Ore a sol |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| without trading | 24 / 24 | 22 | 9 | 33 | 20.4 | 11, all intruders | 89 | 10 % | 28 % | 15.5 |
| **with trading** | **24 / 24** | **24** | **14** | **33** | **23.0** | **21**: 16 intruders, 5 hunger | **107** | **9 %** | **15 %** | **18.9** |

**What changed hands.**

- **Deals:** 122 in 122 attempts, 3–7 a colony. About 186 merchants landed. At the
  others the player had nothing it wanted that it could pay for.
- **Bought:** 660 Metal, 620 Ore, 200 Bioplastic, 90 Food, 75 Spares and 65 Guns.
- **Given:** 2,860 coins, 2,970 Starch, 1,980 Bioplastic, 560 Vegetables and 60 Meat.
- **Value:** 40,610 given at base value for 24,875 taken. The difference is the markup,
  plus lots that overshoot.
- **At sol 40 a colony holds:**

  | | Coins | Metal | Starch |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | without trading | 147 | 112 | 154 |
  | with trading | 30 | 168 | 70 |

- **The store** is full 15 % of the time instead of 28 %. The Starch and Bioplastic
  that filled it are sold.

**The deaths.**

- **More intruders, because more colonies are big.** Intruders land only on colonies of

  - The script put a second oxygen dome in the core site where, without trading, it

  - The canteen it wanted next found no site for ten sols (`PATH BLOCKED`).
  - That left one canteen with one operator for eighteen colonists. The Meals fell six

#### Past thirty-three, at milestone 140

After milestone 139 the user asked to go on. Nothing had been played past 33 colonists,
so the scripted player played 60 sols instead of 40, on the same 24 worlds. **With
milestone 139's player, 14 of 24 colonies were dead by sol 60:** 383 deaths, 354 of them
to hunger.

In every one of those colonies the player had found no site for its next food dome.
It built only small domes, one machine each, and looked for sites within 14 tiles of
the domes' centre.

**What the player does now** (`tools/play.py`, plans `big*`; tweak `nogrow` turns it all
off):

- **It fills before it builds.** A new machine goes into a free slot of a medium or large
  dome of its room that already works (`Game.fill`). That costs one machine, 8 Metal and
  2 Bioplastic, with no site and no corridor.
- **It builds medium domes from fourteen colonists.** This covers the canteen, the
  greenhouses, the lab, the factories, the quarters and the spare-parts factory. A
  medium dome holds four machines for 24 Metal, against one for 12. Medium quarters
  sleep 6, against 2. Where no medium dome fits, it builds a small one.
- **It searches wider.** It looks for a site within 14 tiles of the domes' centre, then
  20, then 26 (`CORE_R`).
- **It builds a second Control** when the colony is within eight of the cap. The cap is
  6 + 48 a Control, up to 80.
- **It builds an ingredient's dome when that ingredient is falling** and covers less than
  five sols. Before, it waited until the ingredient was under ten, when the Meals were
  already falling.
- **It lets a colonist ship in only when the ingredients and the water are not falling**,
  or each covers five sols. With ten sols the colonies stayed at eighteen.
- **It keeps 30 Metal from fourteen colonists**, except for oxygen, water and the second
  airlock. Under 30 the game stops everything that eats Metal ([§6.5](#thirty-metal-kept-at-milestone-127)),
  Spares included. Without the reserve the player held the Metal there 57–65 % of the time.
- **It builds Spares again** when they run low, up to one more factory for each fifteen
  colonists.
- **It builds a second airlock** at sixteen colonists.
- **It builds a medium Storage from the fifth one**, under the game's eight
  ([§6.8](#eight-of-a-kind-measured-at-milestone-140)).

#### Spares kept, at milestone 143

`g142`'s 90 air deaths were `OXYGEN` machines broken with no spares. **The user chose to
change only the player.** The game is milestone 142's, byte for byte, and the batches are
the same 24 worlds and 60 sols.

**Why there were no spares.** In `g142` only 2 colonies of 24 had a `SPARES` machine. The
plan tries its stages in order, and a stage it cannot pay for yet holds back every stage
after it. The first `SPARES` stage was second from last, after "under 6 Spares", so the
food and the storage held it back. The merchant was no backstop either: in the trade
plan Spares came after Metal up to 200, Ore and Guns, and the `1048` and `C0DE` colonies
bought none in 60 sols.

**What changed in `tools/play.py`:**

- **A reserve:** four Spares, and one more for every eight colonists (`spare_res`).
- **The trade:** under the reserve, Spares come first, up to the reserve and four more.
- **The first `SPARES`** fills a free slot of a medium factory if there is one, and is
  an `aside` stage. That means it is tried at every sample, outside the order: it is not
  held back by a stage that cannot pay, and it does not hold others back when it cannot.

Three ways were measured:

| Batch | `SPARES` | Spares at 0 | Mean Spares | `OXYGEN` faults with 0 Spares | Alive at sol 60 | Past twenty | Most | Mean at sol 60 | Deaths: air, hunger, intruders | Mean Metal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `g142` (milestone 142) | 2 / 24 | 7.7 % | 10.8 | 10 of 20 | 22 / 24 | 18 | 46 | 20.2 | 159: 90, 45, 19 | 69.6 |
| `g143`: in order, before the storage, under the reserve | 7 | 5.0 % | 13.2 | 6 of 14 | 22 / 24 | 17 | 46 | 20.5 | 132: 63, 44, 13 | 68.9 |
| `g143b`: aside, from fourteen colonists | 21 | 0.8 % | 75.8 | 0 of 15 | 23 / 24 | **5** | 35 | 17.0 | 25: 0, 19, 6 | 54.0 |
| **`g143c`: aside, under the reserve** | 12 | 2.1 % | 29.3 | 1 of 15 | **24 / 24** | 16 | 38 | **22.7** | **35: 8, 7, 11** | 67.3 |

1. **In order, the stage still came too late.** The Spares fell under the reserve around

**Why there was no fourth pump.** `1048` 0 was replayed to sol 42, and a pump was tried
on every shore within 40 tiles of the ship, one per 4×4 block. Only 2 of 100 took one,
25 tiles north. The domes of the plan `big` had taken the whole shore of the lake beside
the ship. The other shores had no structure within 12 tiles ("too far", 7,673 times). A
pump's path must reach a structure, and the ship does not count
([§9.3](#every-building-needs-a-neighbour-at-milestone-85)). At the start that world had
23 pump sites within 20 tiles: there was land, and the domes took it.

**What changed in `tools/play.py`** (plan `big` only, `Game.keep_shore`):

- **One site kept, from fourteen colonists:** a 3×3 footprint that passes `bd_res`, and

- **Kept with its path:** no dome, structure, corridor or path covers the site or the
  tiles of its path (`on_shore`, `shore_cut`).
- The pump stage tries the kept site first.
- The site is chosen afresh every time the colony changes.

#### Past sixty-four, at milestone 147

No colony had passed 64. The eight largest worlds of `g145f`/`g146` were played for 120
sols with the player of milestone 145 (`g147`). None passed 64, for two reasons:

- **Water.** `1048` 0 (64 colonists) and `5A5A` 2 (36) found no pump site from sol
  57–59. Their water ran out, the `OXYGEN` machines stopped, and 56 and 28 died of air
  at sol 74–75.
- **Room.** The population cap is 6 + 48 per Control, up to 80
  ([§6.1](#colonists-and-bots-at-milestone-92)), so 54 with one.
  Four colonies of 47–54 found no site for a second Control within 26 tiles.

**Only the player changed** (`tools/play.py`). The game is milestone 146's, byte for
byte. Every rule below is the player's:

- **A pump on a far shore** (`far_shore`). When no pump fits, the player looks at every
  shore within 40 tiles, one per 4 × 4, nearest a structure first. The 40 nearest water
  tiles that milestone 145 looked at are all on the lakes the colony already ringed.
- **An airlock as a stepping stone** (`with_airlock`). In `1048` 0 at sol 58, no
  structure of any kind could be placed within 16 tiles of the others: domes,
  corridors and paths had fenced the colony in, and every path was cut. An airlock
  needs no path, since it joins a dome by a corridor. It is still a structure, so it is
  the anchor a pump's path needs. There, 22 airlock sites fitted, and they opened a pump
  site on 17 of 75 shores. The player puts one down only if, in a copy of the colony with
  the airlock and its corridor, a pump then fits within 4 tiles of a shore. Placing it
  "as near the shore as possible" found only water and shore around the shores.
- **The same for power** (`struct_anchor`). With more domes, `1048` 0's solar panels
  found no site from sol 52. Use rose to 253 against 162 made, the pumps stopped, and
  the player built 14 of them. A solar panel, collector or turbine that finds no site
  now gets an airlock at the edge of the colony, where it then fits.
- **Pumps only with power.** No new pump while power was cut for more than half the last
  sol. Without full power a pump stops. Nights are a third.
- **Domes to 32 tiles.** The core zone searches up to 32 tiles (it was 26), so the second
  Control finds a site.
- **Two of the 32 structure slots are kept for pumps.** The game holds 32 structures
  (`MAX_STRUCT`). In `g147h`, `1048` 0 filled them at 79 colonists: 11 solar panels,
  8 airlocks, 7 pumps, 3 collectors, the ship, a mine and the pad. Then the next pump
  would not go in, and the water ran out. All 8 guards were walking to their needs, and
  a guard on the way to a need does not fight ([§6.10](#intruders-at-milestone-111)).
  The raid of sol 94 killed them all, and the next one, at sol 102, killed the other 67.

### 10.2 Milestones

No victory screen — Planetbase's own choice, and the right one for a game about a
colony that either continues or does not.

| Milestone | Requirement | Reachable today? |
|---|---|---|
| Foothold | 10 colonists, all needs green for one sol | ✅ |
| Industry | Metal, Bioplastic and Spares produced on site | ✅ |
| Independence | all ten stocks produced on site; no merchant trade for five sols | ✅ — and since milestone 93 trading is possible, so the second half means something ([§6.11](#trade-at-milestone-93)); since 94 the Ore must be dug ([§6.7](#drilling-at-milestone-94)), and since 95 carried to a store or the ship, where it counts as made ([§6.7](#hauling-at-milestone-95)) |
| Automation | 8 bots | ✅ from milestone 92 — and never before ([below](#automation-at-milestone-92)) |
| Habitat | 80 colonists, independent, five consecutive sols with no deaths | ✅ |

**"All needs green" is the colony's indicator, not every colonist's bar.** With ninety
people somebody is always walking to the canteen, and a milestone that can never be
met is not a milestone. It reads oxygen, power, and whether there is any water and
food at all — which is what a player would see on the HUD.

Everything is counted **once per sol**, in one pass, and never inside the hot slots:
128 agents every 750 revolutions costs nothing. Milestones are sticky; streaks are not.

#### Automation, at milestone 92

**It was never reachable, not even while the ships brought bots.** It counted bots
that were alive *and working* (`F_WORKING`), and `F_WORKING` is set only by the
arrival of an Operate, Heal or Defend job ([§6.7](#67-jobs)) — none of which a bot can
take. A bot builds (Build), carries (Supply, Haul) and drills (Drill), and none of
those sets it. The slot-15 test made its eight bots by writing the flag by hand.

The player chose **eight living bots**, counted at the sol's change over their
sixteen places ([§6.1](#colonists-and-bots-at-milestone-92)), and bots come from the
Bots stock ([§6.11](#bots-at-milestone-92)). `tests/test_bots.py` makes eight from the
stock in the running game and the next sol sets the bit; with seven it does not.
What bots could do then was Build and Supply: Haul and Drill had no publisher, so a
colony's bots worked when there was something to build, and stood in the factory when
there was not. Since milestone 94 driller bots dig, and since 95 carrier bots carry
the mines' Ore ([§6.7](#hauling-at-milestone-95)).

**The sol length is data, not a constant.** A test that wants to watch five sols
cannot wait 60,000 frames, so `sollen` and `daylen` live in the economy record. The
game ships with 12,000 and 7,200.

#### Smaller, at milestone 57

`src/ship.asm` went from 574 bytes to **377**, a third of the file, and slot 15 got
faster where it does any work: a colonist landing 4,300 → 3,710 µs, visitors
4,220 → 4,000, the sol 3,850 → 2,450. Nothing else changed.

That was checked with a script kept out of the repository. It runs slot 15 pinned
through 93 states with the old file and the new one:

- a ship in every state, and an ETA that needs both bytes;
- colonists with the cap at every distance from full, and with two free agent ids
  or none;
- visitors with 100, 6, 5 and no Food;
- the visitor roll with the pad free, taken, and missing;
- each streak's condition, at 254 and 255;
- bots by count, role and flags;
- 33 production masks against three no-trade streaks;
- each Habitat condition on both sides of its line.

Every state came out byte for byte the same, the sound included, and the same as the
reference.

- **The milestones' goods are two constant masks.** Industry's three goods and
  Independence's ten went in as lists. A loop then rebuilt each bit with shifts every
  sol, and a routine compared them one by one. Now Industry is an `and`/`cp` on the
  low byte of `EC_PRODM`. Independence is "`(high | &FC) & low` is 255".
- **The milestones go straight into `EC_MILE`.** Each one is a `set n,(hl)`, with
  `HL` held on the byte. Habitat reads Independence with `bit`, including a bit set
  in the same sol. The copy (`sh_mile`), the routine that ORed into it, and the
  bots' counter in memory are gone.
- **The three streaks are one routine.** It takes a pointer to the counter and the
  zero flag: Z continues (+1, up to 255), NZ breaks (0). The sol's deaths and trades
  are read, cleared and turned into that flag. The streaks sit side by side, which an
  `assert` holds.
- **A new colonist is a table:** the six pages after the flags, low half and high
  half each. `ship_crew` writes the pad's node into the table. It also counts every
  birth into `EC_ALIVE` at once, so every exit finds the count right — the bug
  milestone 38 fixed can no longer be written.
- **Smaller pieces:**
  - "INCOMING → LANDED, LANDED → gone" is `add a,a / and 3`.
  - The visitors' Food is read and written at its own address, not through
    `ec_stock_ptr`.
  - Kind and state are written as one word in `ship_call`.

**The reference had a bug of its own.** `tools/econ.py` counted the green streak
without the ceiling the other two have. A colony on its 255th green sol would have
made it overflow the byte that `to_bytes` writes, which raised an error. The Z80 had
always stopped at 255. No test had come near 255 sols; the script above did.

**What the planted faults found.** Fifteen faults were run, one in each branch:

- The script caught all fifteen.
- `test_sim.py` caught five.
- `test_game.py` caught none.

Ten passed every test. `test_game.py` lands its four colonists on a colony with a cap
of 52 and four people, and its `C` key checks for the pad before `ship_call` does. The
ten were:

- the pad check in `ship_call`;
- the visitors' Food going below zero;
- morale running over 255;
- the population cap;
- a streak passing 255;
- bots counted from role 4;
- Automation from nine bots;
- Industry without Spares;
- Independence without the tenth good;
- Habitat reading the wrong milestone.

They are cases in `test_sim.py` now (`SHIP_CASES`), Z80 against the reference with
slot 15 pinned. Each of the ten faults fails it at its own case. The old `ship.asm`
passes it, negative included.

### 10.3 Failure

Every colonist dead. No other loss condition — a colony at 2 population with no power is
technically alive, and being allowed to try to save it is the point.

### 10.4 Time

| | |
|---|---|
| Frame | 20 ms |
| Wheel revolution | 16 frames = 320 ms |
| Sol | 4 minutes = 12,000 frames = 750 revolutions |
| Night | ≈ 40% of a sol |
| A full game | 40–80 sols, 3–5 hours |

## 11. Save and load

Three slots on disc, written by the game's own FDC routines — AMSDOS cannot be used,
because its workspace at `&A700–&BFFF` is occupied by bank 2 data. **Built**: `S`
and `L` open a slot chooser, both only from `LOOK`.

| Sector | Section | Bytes |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Header: magic, version, seed, planet, camera, cursor, slot | 512 |
| 1–32 | **World plane, verbatim** — bank 4 | 16,384 |
| 33–41 | Agents, domes, structures, slot occupancy, seed — bank 6 `&6C00–&7DFF` (and the corridors until milestone 154) | 4,608 |
| 42 | **Corridors** — bank 5 `&7800–&79FF`, since milestone 154: 388 bytes of records and 124 free ones | 512 |
| 43–46 | Economy, job board, node graph, `LK_OWN` — bank 2, the 2 KB under `hud_shadow` (`&8F00–&96FF` since milestone 90; `&A400` until 33); sectors 42–45 until milestone 154 | 2,048 |
| | **Total** | **24,064** |

The world plane **is** saved, in full. Regenerating it from the seed would cost
5.1 s on every load (13.5 until milestone 112) ([§5.10](#510-player-modification)); the 46 sectors (47 since milestone 154) cost
**0.7 s measured in the emulator** (`tests/test_save.py`), plus 0.46 s for the motor
to come up to speed since milestone 113 ([below](#on-a-real-drive-at-milestone-113)) —
real hardware will be several times that, because the emulator has no rotational
latency and a real drive waits for each sector to come round.

**Nothing derived is saved**, and that is the rule that makes the file this small:
not `NEXTHOP` (12 KB, rebuilt by the wheel), not the figure cache (rebuilt from the
agents), not the dirty list, not the wheel's position. Loading rebuilds all of it in
the same order a new game does — `wheel_reset`, `rt_mark`, `dirty_reset`, `gh_reset`,
then a full draw. Since milestone 115 the load enters through `wheel_load`, which also
raises `jb_lost`: the first flow cycle looks for site jobs a full board dropped
before the save, since the flag is not saved ([§6.7](#nothing-waits-for-a-full-board-at-milestone-115)). `NEXTHOP` is **zeroed** first, exactly as the loader leaves it at
boot ([§13.1](#131-three-ways-a-loader-does-not-run)): a stale next-hop is not
garbage, it is a *valid neighbour of another world*, and an agent reading one walks
off in a direction that made sense in a game that no longer exists.

**Where on the disc.** A slot is 6 tracks (54 sectors, 46 used, 47 since milestone 154) and the three live at
tracks 24, 30 and 36 — the disc holds 42. `sv_save` and `sv_load` take a slot number,
and **all three are now reachable**: `S` and `L` no longer save and load on the spot,
they open a one-line chooser in the panel — `SAVE TO SLOT 2`, left and right to
change, `FIRE` to go, `ESC` to back out. The choice is *remembered*, because a player
who saves into slot 3 usually saves into slot 3 again. Until milestone 22 the UI
passed `xor a` and two of the three slots — 46 KB of disc — had never been written by
anything, test included; `tests/test_save.py` now writes slot 3 (tracks 36–41), reads
slot 1 back to prove it was untouched, and reads slot 3 back to prove it holds its own
game. They belong to no AMSDOS file: this is the game's own disc, `tools/mkdsk.py`
checks at build time that no file reaches track 24, and a save that overwrote one
would be silent otherwise.

The header is checked **before** a single byte of the game is overwritten. An empty
slot is `&E5` from end to end — perfectly valid bytes, an invalid game — and without
the magic, *load* on an untouched slot would fill the world with rubbish and hang the
simulation. `tests/test_save.py` loads from an empty slot on purpose and asserts that
nothing moves. An empty slot now **says so** — `NOTHING IN SLOT 2`, not `DISC ERROR`;
`sv_hdr_ok` returns `&FF` and the controller returns anything else, so the two are
told apart at no cost.

**And a message stays on screen for two seconds.** It used to live until the next
`ml_hud`, sixteen frames away. A save takes two seconds of disc, so its message was
visible the whole time by accident; a rejected empty slot is decided in one seek and
the player saw a flash. `ui_msg` sets a counter that `ui_panel` decrements instead of
repainting — six HUD ticks, sixteen bytes of code.

**The version is 10 since milestone 154, and was 9 from milestone 111** (`SV_VER`); a
save of another version is refused, not misread. 9 adds the landings' count to the economy (`EC_LANDS`,
[§6.11](#611-ships-and-arrivals)), 107 → 108 bytes. Everything after it moved by one,
into the last byte of the gap before `rt_nodes`, which is now full. The intruders
themselves are agents 96–99, in the block the save already holds. A load sets `fo_n`
to `&80`, so the next revolution counts them, and `tests/test_save.py` checks both.
**Milestone 149 kept 9**: the tutorial's step, `EC_TU`, is agent 121's byte of
`node_occ`, in the entities' block, which every earlier save holds as 0 — and 0 is
"no tutorial" unless `worldinfo` says the world is the tutorial's, which no earlier
save can ([§9.6](#96-the-tutorial-at-milestone-149)). A load ends with `tu_run`, which
puts the line and both bytes of self-modified code back as the loaded game wants them.
**Milestone 150 kept 9**: the guards' rule reads the task and the flags every save holds
([§6.10](#guards-leave-their-needs-for-the-fight-at-milestone-150)).
**Version 10 came with milestone 154**: the corridors are 4 bytes in bank 5, a block of
their own (one sector), the domes, the structures and `node_occ` moved inside bank 6's
block, and `LK_OWN` moved and changed its encoding ([§4.2](#corridors-in-bank-5-and-the-structures-on-two-pages-at-milestone-154)). A save of 9
would be misread in all four, so it is refused.
8 came with milestone 94 and adds the finished mines to the economy (`EC_MINES`), 106 → 107
bytes, so everything after it moved by one, into the gap before `rt_nodes`, which has
one left; and the seventh byte of a mine counts who digs there, with bit 7 for its
Drill job ([§6.7](#drilling-at-milestone-94)). **Milestone 95 kept 8**: a mine's pile
is its eighth byte and its Haul bit 6 of the seventh, both in the structure table the
save already holds, and a save of 94 loads with every pile empty and every Haul to be
posted. **Milestone 102 kept 8 too**: where each structure's link goes is one byte in
`node_deg`'s unused entries 96–127, inside the block, and a save of 101 loads with all of
them 0 — its paths stay as they were when one of their ends is demolished
([§9.3](#paths-that-go-at-milestone-102)). **Milestone 103 kept 8**: only where the code
that saves lives moved ([below](#where-the-code-is-since-milestone-103)). So did 104, which
changed only what an impact does to the people on their way to an airlock. **And
milestone 121 kept 9**: the calm's two timestamps are six bytes in `node_occ`'s
unused entries for agents 100–127, inside bank 6's block, and a save of 120 loads with
them 0, which reads as *never* — the next roll may bring a disaster at once
([§6.10](#sparse-and-not-before-twenty-colonists-at-milestone-121)). **So did 122**: the
storage's flag is not saved. `wheel_load` clears it through `wheel_reset`, and the first
flow cycle, at most 64 revolutions later, counts again ([§6.5](#storage-at-milestone-122)).
**And 123**: a mine's two new bits in `ST_OPS`, half yield and free, read 0 from an older
save, which means full yield and paid ([§6.5](#a-mine-anywhere-at-milestone-123)).
**And 136**: the walking visitors are agents 112–119 and the count of those inside one
byte of `node_occ`'s upper half, all in bank 6's block; a save of 135 loads with no
visitor, and a visitor ship it had landed leaves at the next revolution
([§6.11](#visitors-who-walk-at-milestone-136)). **And milestone 157 kept 10**: the
structures' scan limit is five bytes in `node_deg`'s unused entries 112–116, inside the
graph's block, and `wheel_load` counts it again from the table through `wheel_reset`
before anything reads it; a save of 156 loads with zeros there and comes out with its
own limit ([§4.2](#the-scan-limit-at-milestone-157)).
7 added the merchant's markup and cargo to the economy, 97 → 106
bytes, which moved the job board, the room index and `src/crew.asm`'s work area by
nine — into the gap before `rt_nodes`, which had exactly eleven; the save test
changes the cargo after saving and checks the load brings back the saved one.
6 is 5's layout with other meanings: ids 80–95 are bots without
needs, and a save of 91 with more than 80 colonists would hand some of them over as
bots. 5 added the ships' shares (`EC_LAND`) to the economy, 92 → 97
bytes, which moved the job board and the room index by five; `tests/test_save.py`'s
table has the new places, and the save test now changes the shares after saving and
checks the load brings back the saved ones. 4 came with milestone 90. 2 came with milestone 33's bank-2 layout, 3 with milestone 87's
meanings (`F_INDOORS`, corridors to a site that are not edges, `ST_JOINED`). Milestone
89 moved the economy inside the bank-2 block, from its first byte to its 109th, with
the machines' operator flags now in front of it, **without** a new version — a
save from 88 would have loaded its stocks from the wrong place and said nothing.
Milestone 90 moved it again, by six bytes, and turned `skill` into the suit. The
block's address comes from `hud_shadow` in the layout, so the game is never wrong
about its *own* saves; what it cannot see is that an older save means something
else. So `tests/test_save.py` now holds the format of each version — where every
table of the two saved blocks is — and fails when the build's layout differs from
the one its `SV_VER` names: with version 3 written as milestone 88 had it, milestone
89's layout fails. And it saves a game stamped `SV_VER − 1`, loads it, and checks it
is refused with nothing touched; with `sv_hdr_ok`'s comparison taken out, the same
save loads.

The seed survives the generator in four bytes of bank 6 (`worldinfo`), written by
`GEN.BIN` before the game's code exists. Without them the running game has no idea
which seed built its world, because the generator is a separate loadable that is
overwritten by bank 2's data ([§13](#13-build-and-test)).

#### Where the code is, since milestone 103

`src/save.asm` and the disc's driver, `src/fdc.asm`, are not in bank 2's code area any
more. They are 646 bytes (630 until milestone 113) of the routing matrix's holes in bank 1, after the demolition's
([§4.2](#memory-again-at-milestone-103)), and run in the ghost's log, as the demolition
does: the log already lent its first 512 bytes to the header (`SV_HDR`), and the code
runs right after them, at `SV_ORG = GH_BUF + 512`. `S` and `L` hide the ghost before
they start (`ui_dosave`, `ui_doload`), so the log is empty.

`sv_save` and `sv_load` keep their names and their place in bank 2 (`src/demolish.asm`):
each copies the 21 rows (20 until milestone 113) to `SV_ORG` and calls in (`svo_save`, `svo_load`). The copy is
made on every `S` and every `L`, because a demolition or a ghost in between writes over
the log. A load used to show the cursor again from inside; it now does that in
`sv_load`, after the code has returned, since showing the ghost writes its log in
`GH_BUF`, under the code that would still be running. A save still took 35 frames and a
load 54 (`tests/test_save.py`), and the format did not change. Since milestone 113 they
take 57 and 74: the motor's start.

#### On a real drive, at milestone 113

The emulator's controller is kinder than a CPC's in three ways, and the driver had
leaned on all three. Milestone 113's loader was written against the real controller
([§13.3](#133-the-loader-reads-the-disc-itself-at-milestone-113)), and the same three
things were wrong in `src/fdc.asm`:

- **Every transfer ends "abnormally" on a CPC.** The µPD765's TC pin is not wired, so
  the controller never learns the transfer is over. It runs to EOT and reports
  IC = 01 (ST0 `&40`) with EN (ST1 bit 7, end of cylinder). That *is* success on a
  real machine. The emulator reports IC = 00, and `fd_end` accepted only IC = 00:
  on a real 6128 every save would have said `DISC ERROR`. `fd_ok` now fails on
  IC = 1x, on NR (ST0 bit 3) and on any bit of ST1 or ST2 except EN.
- **The motor waited 21 ms.** The comment said half a second, which is what a drive
  needs to come up to speed, and the loop was `&0C00` × 7 µs. It is 65,536 × 7 µs =
  0.46 s now (AMSDOS waits 1 s). This is the whole cost: 21 frames on a save, 20 on a
  load.
- **The seek waited about 8 ms.** `fdc_seek` asked `SENSE INTERRUPT STATUS` at most
  100 times. A head step takes 12 ms and the slots are 24 tracks in, so on a real
  drive the first read or write would have started with the head still moving. It
  now asks up to 40 × 256 times, about a second; the emulator's head arrives at once.

All three fit in 16 bytes, in the 18 the ghost's log had left. `tests/test_disc.py`
checks `fd_ok` with the result bytes themselves, nine cases, from the running game:
the emulator's `&00`, the CPC's `&40 &80`, and ND, a CRC error, a missing address
mark, deleted data, not ready, an invalid command and IC = 11. The check as it was
until milestone 112 fails the CPC's case, and one that accepts ND fails the ND case.
The timings cannot be tested here; they are listed in [§15](#15-open-risks).

**ASSET-3, 4, 5 and 6 are delivered too.** Every asset gap in this table is now
closed, and [§4.2](#42-the-eight-banks) shows every bank fitting. The rows are kept
with their sizes because the memory map in
[§4.3](#43-bank-2-flat-again) is built on those numbers.

| # | Asset | Size | Why |
